items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: I only have one Milt Hinton story, because I didn’t really know him.

ctx.x: Do you have a Milt Hinton story?

I only have one Milt Hinton story, because I didn’t really know him. But one day I was entering the musicians union and I had my bass and I had an amplifier I think, at the same time. And it was like one of those days in New York where it was like 200 degrees and humid. And I went through the door of the union and I hit the cold air and I was like ahhh man. It just felt great to have the air conditioning finally descend upon me. And I hear this guy say, “hey man, what’s the matter with you?” He said, “when I came…

wasn’t any air conditioning in this building.” And I looked up and it was Milt. He had the hat and everything else. I go, “are you Milt Hinton?” “That’s right.” He was nice. I chatted with him very briefly. But I did know he’s clearly a great bass player. There are a lot of great stories about him. And the other guy from that era who is unbelievable is George Duvivier. George played on zillions of records. I knew him a little bit. I subbed for him a couple of times back in you know, 1982. And there’s another bass…
